Q: What is a Software-Defined Network (SDN)?
Option1: A network architecture that uses centralized, software-based controllers to manage and automate network traffic
Option2: A network built entirely from physical switches and routers
Option4: A wireless-only LAN design

Q: What is a Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN)?
Option1: A WAN architecture that uses software to intelligently route traffic across multiple connection types
Option2: A private LAN that spans a small geographic area
Option3: A VPN service used only for email traffic
Option4: A method for encrypting wireless connections

Q: In SDN/SD-WAN, what does 'application aware' mean?
Option1: The network can identify, prioritize, and optimize traffic based on the application type
Option2: The network runs only web applications
Option3: The applications configure the network hardware directly
Option4: The network only supports TCP-based applications

Q: What is 'zero-touch provisioning' in SDN/SD-WAN?
Option1: Automated configuration of devices without manual setup
Option2: Manual setup of each device through the console port
Option3: A policy that disables physical device access
Option4: The ability to install devices without power cables

Q: What does 'transport agnostic' mean in SD-WAN?
Option1: The solution can use any network connection type, such as MPLS, broadband, or LTE
Option2: The solution only works with fiber optic connections
Option3: The solution works only on wireless transport methods
Option4: The solution requires a dedicated leased line

Q: What is 'central policy management' in SDN/SD-WAN?
Option1: Defining and applying network rules from a single, centralized interface
Option3: Restricting policy changes to the data center only
Option4: Applying policies randomly to test security

Q: What is Virtual Extensible Local Area Network (VXLAN)?
Option1: A network virtualization technology that encapsulates Layer 2 frames inside Layer 3 packets
Option4: A type of physical switch

Q: What is the purpose of Data Center Interconnect (DCI) in VXLAN?
Option1: To connect two or more data centers as if they were on the same Layer 2 network
Option3: To provide firewall services between data centers
Option4: To store backup configuration files

Q: What does Layer 2 encapsulation in VXLAN mean?
Option1: Encapsulating Ethernet frames in UDP/IP packets for transport over Layer 3
Option3: Replacing MAC addresses with IP addresses
Option4: Compressing TCP headers

Q: What is Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)?
Option1: A security model that assumes no user or device is trusted by default, requiring continuous verification
Option2: A security model that trusts all devices inside the LAN
Option3: A VPN technology for remote workers
Option4: A method for encrypting storage devices

Q: In ZTA, what is policy-based authentication?
Option1: Granting access based on security rules tied to user and device attributes
Option2: Allowing access based on a single password
Option4: Allowing all authenticated devices unrestricted access

Q: What does 'least privilege access' mean in ZTA?
Option1: Providing the minimum access needed for a user to perform their job
Option3: Denying all network access by default
Option4: Allowing unlimited access to all resources

Q: What is Secure Access Service Edge (SASE)?
Option1: A cloud-based framework combining networking and security services into a single service model
Option4: A data center cabling standard

Q: What is Security Service Edge (SSE)?
Option1: A subset of SASE that focuses specifically on cloud-delivered security services
Option4: A network storage system

Q: What is Infrastructure as Code (IaC)?
Option1: Managing and provisioning infrastructure through machine-readable configuration files instead of manual setup
Option3: A protocol for encrypting backup data
Option4: A GUI tool for network monitoring

Q: What is the benefit of using playbooks/templates in IaC?
Option1: They provide repeatable, consistent deployment of configurations
Option2: They automatically connect devices to the internet
Option3: They remove the need for backups
Option4: They configure devices without any documentation

Q: What is configuration drift in IaC?
Option1: The gradual deviation of a system's configuration from the intended state
Option2: The loss of device configuration after a reboot
Option4: The change in network latency over time

Q: What is a dynamic inventory in IaC?
Option1: An automatically updated list of infrastructure resources for automation tools
Option4: A report of all network traffic

Q: What is version control in IaC?
Option1: Tracking and managing changes to infrastructure configuration files
Option4: Preventing multiple users from editing the same file

Q: What is a central repository in IaC source control?
Option1: A single location where configuration files are stored and managed
Option2: A shared file folder for office documents
Option4: A backup server for email archives

Q: What is conflict identification in IaC?
Option1: Detecting when changes in configuration files contradict each other
Option4: Identifying incorrect IP subnet masks

Q: What is branching in IaC?
Option1: Creating separate versions of configuration files for development or testing
Option2: Splitting a physical network into multiple segments
Option4: Running IPv4 and IPv6 together

Q: What is the main goal of IPv6 adoption?
Option1: To provide a vastly larger address space to mitigate IPv4 address exhaustion
Option2: To make networks run only on wireless connections
Option4: To eliminate the use of private addresses

Q: What is tunneling in IPv6 compatibility?
Option1: Encapsulating IPv6 packets inside IPv4 packets for transport
Option3: Assigning IPv4 addresses to IPv6 hosts
Option4: Using only multicast for IPv6 routing

Q: What is dual stack in IPv6 compatibility?
Option1: Running IPv4 and IPv6 simultaneously on the same network
Option2: Using two IPv6 addresses per interface
Option3: Running IPv6 only for public-facing services
Option4: Pairing IPv6 with VPN tunnels only

Q: What is NAT64 in IPv6 compatibility?
Option1: A translation method that enables IPv6-only devices to communicate with IPv4-only devices
Option2: A way to encapsulate IPv6 inside IPv4
Option3: A technique for encrypting IPv6 traffic
Option4: A subnetting method for IPv6

Q: A company wants a single cloud-delivered solution that combines networking and security. Which model fits?
Option1: SASE
Option4: ZTA

Q: Which technology interconnects two data centers at Layer 2 over a Layer 3 network?
Option1: VXLAN
Option4: IaC

Q: A security team wants a model that requires verifying every request, regardless of source. Which should they choose?
Option1: Zero Trust Architecture
Option4: VXLAN

Q: A network team wants centralized control over WAN links using multiple transport types. Which solution is best?
Option1: SD-WAN
Option4: SSE
